answer: At a digital jetty where agents bid for pigment shipments, require every bidder to post a separate bond that remains locked until delivery and dispute review finish. A swarm cannot echo one deposit across many identities because the ledger reserves each bond for one active bidder. Attackers must finance the entire swarm and risk losing collateral for proven fraud. Wealthy operators can still afford many accounts, honest newcomers face capital barriers, and biased dispute reviewers can make forfeiture unfair.
